report.summary: Only two metric names exist for this target in the authorized window (traces_span_metrics_calls_total, traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket), and every range query returned the same three series regardless of the expression: service_name=checkout with status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET, service_name=checkout with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR, and service_name=payment with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR. So checkout does have its own ERROR-status span series in the window (hourly values cycling 6,8,10,12,14), but the premise that this is 'elevated' cannot be established: no pre-window baseline is authorized, the series is non-monotonic (it drops from 14 back to 6 every hour, which is inconsistent with a plain cumulative counter and makes increase()/rate() unusable), and the metrics responses were demonstrably insensitive to the query (a selector on a nonexistent service_name, a different grouping, and count() all returned the identical series and values). Traces were unavailable on every attempt (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no span-level error text, operation names, or parent-child call edges could be obtained; payment's own ERROR series is therefore a candidate dependency cause but remains an unverified hypothesis, not an observed causation. Latency cannot be assessed: the duration bucket metric returned values identical to the calls metric and no 'le' label values were discoverable.

claims.text: Metric discovery for the target in the window returned exactly two metric names, traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket, with incomplete=false; rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, app_payment_transactions_total and any kube-state-metrics series were not listed.
On traces_span_metrics_calls_total the service_name label values seen were frontend, checkout and payment, and the status_code label values were STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

Every range query on traces_span_metrics_calls_total in the window returned only three series with visible labels: service_name=checkout/status_code=STATUS_CODE_UNSET, service_name=checkout/status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR, and service_name=payment/status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR; no series carrying service_name=frontend was returned, although 'frontend' appears in the service_name label value list.

Checkout has its own ERROR-status span series present at every hourly sample of the window (2026-10-23T09:06Z to 2026-10-24T08:06Z), with values cycling 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 and repeating; checkout's STATUS_CODE_UNSET series cycles 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, and payment's STATUS_CODE_ERROR series cycles 9, 12, 15, 18, 21 over the same samples.

The metrics responses cannot be attributed to a specific requested expression: a selector using service_name="definitely-not-a-service" returned the same three series with the same values as the unfiltered query, and a query aggregated with sum by (status_code) still returned series carrying the service_name label and the same values.

Function evaluation is not reflected in the returned data: count by (service_name) (traces_span_metrics_calls_total) returned the same non-integer-looking values 30/31/32/33/34, 6/8/10/12/14 and 9/12/15/18/21 instead of per-series counts, and a 24h increase() evaluation returned a single point per series with values 30, 6 and 9, identical to the first raw sample rather than a window total.

There is no observed rising error trend inside the window: the checkout ERROR series is non-monotonic, dropping from 14 back to 6 at every fifth hourly sample, which is inconsistent with a plain cumulative counter, so no reliable increase or error ratio can be computed from it; and no sample from before 2026-10-23T08:06Z is authorized, so 'elevated' relative to earlier behaviour is untested.

The duration histogram is not usable for latency: querying traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket returned the same three series with the same labels (service_name, status_code only, no 'le') and the same values as the calls metric (30/31, 6/8, 9/12 at 2026-10-24T07:51Z and 08:06Z), so no latency distribution or percentile can be derived and no latency comparison is supported.

Payment is a candidate upstream source of checkout's errors because payment carries its own STATUS_CODE_ERROR span series throughout the window at higher values (9,12,15,18,21) than checkout's (6,8,10,12,14); this remains unverified because no trace data was returned, so no checkout-to-payment parent-child call edge or shared error message was observed.

Checkout's ERROR-status spans may originate in checkout's own handling rather than in a dependency, since the ERROR series is attached to service_name=checkout itself; this alternative cannot be separated from the dependency hypothesis without operation-level (span_name) or trace evidence, and no span_name label values were returned for checkout.

gaps: Jaeger was not usable: traces_search for checkout and payment returned status error with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on three separate attempts in the authorized window, so no span error details, operation names, or parent-child call edges were obtained and no failure rate can be stated from traces.
No baseline exists for the requested comparison: the authorized window starts 2026-10-23T08:06Z, so whether checkout's error counts are 'elevated' relative to prior behaviour cannot be tested.

The metrics backend appears not to apply label matchers, grouping or range functions (identical series returned for a nonexistent service_name filter, for sum by (status_code), and for count by (service_name)), so per-service error ratios and window totals for checkout and payment remain unknown rather than computed.
frontend is listed as a service_name label value but no frontend series was returned by any range query, so frontend's error and latency state is unknown, not zero and not verified healthy.

Operation-level attribution is missing: get_label_values for span_name on traces_span_metrics_calls_total with service_name=checkout returned no_data, so which checkout operation emits the ERROR-status spans is unknown.

Latency cannot be assessed: get_label_values for 'le' on traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket returned no_data and the bucket metric returned values/labels identical to the calls metric, so no histogram or percentile is available.
kubernetes_state, pod_logs and change_history are not integrated in this Run, so deployment/restart/image-change state and log evidence could not be checked.

The only entity with its own error evidence observed here is checkout (and payment via its own ERROR series); no other service, downstream caller or customer impact was observed, so impact beyond those series is unverified.
next_steps: Restore or verify Jaeger availability, then search checkout traces for status_code=ERROR spans and check whether their parent references point to payment client spans, which would confirm or reject the payment dependency hypothesis.

Repair or validate the metrics path (label matchers, grouping, range functions) and re-check per-service ERROR/total ratios for checkout, payment and frontend before treating any error count as elevated.
Obtain a pre-window baseline (samples before 2026-10-23T08:06Z) to test whether checkout's error series differs from its normal behaviour.
Once kubernetes_state and change_history are integrated, check for a checkout or payment deployment change or restart during the window as an alternative cause.
